messages:
ian (eng-platform): quick heads-up — i'm starting a short RFC follow-up on enrichment windowing + tenant cohort strategy. trying to capture tradeoffs for cost attribution vs cardinality. cc @maria @samira

maria (eng-ml): curious, can you sketch the concrete proposal? high-level is fine.

ian (eng-platform): yeah. gist: keep a small set of tenant-level identifiers on the envelope (tenant_id, tenant_cohort_hash) that are always present. push higher-cardinality attributes (service_cohort, feature_flag_snapshot, per-route) into the enrichment stage where we can window and sample. goal: accurate per-tenant cost buckets without exploding storage/ingest.

david (eng-platform): big +1 on envelope-minimalism. but watch chargeback/reporting needs — finance wants per-feature cost attribution monthly, not probabilistic. how do we support that?

samira (eng-infra): two quick angles: 1) retention & windowing: if enrichment runs async, you lose exact arrival ordering which matters for short windows. 2) sampling: we can keep deterministic sampling keyed by tenant_cohort_hash to allow unbiased estimates for high-cardinality attrs.

maria (eng-ml): deterministic sampling + cohorting could work for ML metrics. but product needs exact counts for billing in some cases. maybe a hybrid: store exact counters for billing tags (low-cardinality) and sampled enriched events for feature-level telemetry.

ian (eng-platform): agree hybrid. propose: envelope has: tenant_id, billing_bucket_id, tenant_cohort_v1. enrichment writes: service_cohort_vN, feature_tag_set (high-card). we persist billing_bucket_id on cold storage with full retention; enriched high-cardinality payloads are TTL'd faster and sampled.

samira (eng-infra): sketch of schema (pseudo):
```json
{
  "envelope": {"tenant_id":"T123","billing_bucket":"B-2024-07","tenant_cohort":"c78f"},
  "enrichment": {"service_cohort":"sc-45","feature_tags":["A","B"],"sample_rate":0.01}
}
```
Note: sample_rate carried so downstream estimates can be scaled.

david (eng-platform): how do we handle retroactive rollups? product may ask "how did cost change if we change cohort logic?" we need versioning.

ian (eng-platform): good call. include cohort_version on envelope + enrichment. cohort_version is small and cheap to store (e.g., v1, v2). we then can re-run rollups deterministically for billing windows using archived envelopes + cohort version mapping.

maria (eng-ml): ops note: re-run requires raw envelope retention. we can't TTL envelopes too aggressively if we want deterministic backfills. maybe store envelopes for billing retention length and keep enriched payloads short-lived.

samira (eng-infra): operational constraints: ingest pipeline amplification if we attach enrichment before fanout. prefer enrichment consumer downstream of fanout so we can shard by tenant and limit hot-tenants. also add backpressure safeguards.

ingest-bot: deploy scheduled: enrichment-consumer-v3 -> canary at 10% starting 2024-09-15 15:00 UTC :robot_face:

ian (eng-platform): next steps i propose: 1) draft small RFC with schema proposal (envelope fields, cohort_version, sample semantics) 2) list retention SLAs for envelopes vs enrichments 3) define backwards-compatible cohort migration plan (v1->v2 rollouts + re-run path) 4) run a quick cost-sim using 30d traffic sample to estimate cardinality impact.

david (eng-platform): okay, i'll take the cost-sim. samira, can you enumerate infra constraints (fanout, backpressure, shard keys)?

samira (eng-infra): yes — i'll list constraints and suggested shard key (tenant_id or billing_bucket for hot-splitting) and plug into RFC. also add deterministic-sampling impl notes (hash algo, seed).

maria (eng-ml): i'll write how sampling affects evals and recommend thresholds where we should disable sampling for certain cohorts.

ian (eng-platform): awesome. i'll open the RFC draft tomorrow and ping this thread. thanks y'all :thumbsup:
